profile-evaluation-report.html:
Free tools›Your application
Your application

Profile evaluation report

Where you actually stand, and what moves you.

Thirty-seven questions, about six minutes. In return: your position on seven dimensions, a reading of how crowded your own applicant pool is and what that changes, all 1,295 programmes we hold sorted into not currently eligible, dream, competitive, safe or not enough published to place — with the school’s own sentence and URL behind every call — and an ordered plan where each action states how many programmes it actually moves.

  • Pool competitiveness
  • Seven dimensions
  • 1,295 programmes placed
  • Every call sourced
  • Counterfactual actions

How this one works

Runs
In your browser
Cost
Free
Sign-up
Not needed
Sources
Named, and the gaps counted

Nothing you type is uploaded unless you press a button that tells you, first, exactly what it sends. Where a figure was not published, this tool leaves a blank rather than a guess — and it prints, at the top of itself, how much of its own data is still missing. That count is the honest one, not this panel.

Profile evaluation report

Where this stops, and a person starts

This tool answers what can be answered from published facts. It will not tell you which school to pick, how to frame the two years you would rather not explain, or what your story actually is — those are judgement, and judgement is what the consultants do.

Involve has placed candidates into programmes across the schools in this data. If you want the judgement layer on top of the facts above, that conversation is free too.

post-study-work-visa.html:

Visa and post-study work rights

Answered for the passport you actually hold.

How long each country lets you stay after you graduate, what you can do in that window, and what you switch onto next — for your nationality, not for a generic international student. An EU passport means several of these countries need no post-study permit at all. An Indian passport is worth an extra year in Australia and a decade in the American green card queue. 173 nationalities, 27 sourced nationality rules, and an honest “no rule found” where there is no difference.

__landing__.title: Free Tools
__landing__.html:
Free tools
Thirteen tools, free, no sign-up

Thirteen tools. One job each.

Pick one below, or use the Free Tools menu at the top of any page.

These are the parts of applying abroad that can be answered from published facts: what a programme requires, what a country costs, what your passport changes, what is still open today. Every figure carries the URL it was read from, and where a school or a government did not publish something, you get a blank rather than a guess. The judgement — which school, which story, which two years to explain — is what the consultants are for.

  • 1,295 programmes
  • 805 institutions
  • 50 countries
  • 173 nationalities
  • Every figure sourced
  • Nothing uploaded

Admission chance %
Never
Rankings
Not used
Your data sold
No
Account required
No
